key_insight: A PatternBoost-based learning-guided search can automate the discovery of new extremal geometric constructions, and modest expert seeding can further improve the best-known integrality-gap bounds.
engineering_relevance: The work provides a practical blueprint for using machine learning to accelerate lower-bound construction and hardness-instance generation in combinatorial optimization and algorithm design.
method: Adapt PatternBoost to geometric instance spaces with custom candidate representations and local search moves.
Use a transformer surrogate to rank candidate constructions before exact verification.
Combine automated search with structured expert-provided seeds to expand instance diversity and escape early plateaus.
evidence_signal: On stabbing unit squares by axis-parallel lines, the method improved the best known lower bound from 3/2 to 20/13, and with a structured staircase seed reached 14/9.
watch_item: Performance appears sensitive to representation design and initial diversity, so naive setups plateau quickly and may miss stronger constructions without domain-specific guidance.
paper_title: Towards Learning-Guided Discovery of Extremal Geometric Constructions: A PatternBoost Study
